- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model persists in upward trend — reduce forecast slope or add downward bias of 2–5%.
- If sentiment history shows increasing negativity (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or 0.20), model tends to ignore sentiment and overconfidently forecasts upward — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per negative sentiment day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle corrections — if true outcome drops sharply after day 15–20, reduce forecast by 2–5% for days 20–30.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows volatility, model underestimates risk — add 1–2% volatility buffer or adjust for sentiment-driven volatility spikes.
